newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas erodes on softer futures, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas erodes on softer futures, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices continued their retreat Monday as milder-than-expected weather blanketed most of the U.S. and lower demand was expected ahead of the holiday, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices lost about 40 cents to the low-$3.90s, with deals done on either side of this range.
The largest factor contributing to the downward trend, traders said, was the revised forecast in Texas and Oklahoma.
Temperatures in the southern plains are forecast to remain above-normal through the week, with the warmest temperatures expected to arrive Friday.
NYMEX January Henry Hub fell early to a low of $4.05 per mmBtu but has since rebounded to $4.28 at 1317 EST.
In the East, temperatures are expected to hover around normal through the week despite last week's threats of a cold front.

As a result of the revised forecast in the Northeast, prices at the New York city-gate were around $4.40 early but then fell into the $4.20s and teens. Most deals, traders said, were done in the high-$4.20 to about $4.30.
Despite sporadic patches of bitterly cold weather, Midcontinent prices plummeted into the $3.90s early and then the $3.60s late, with most deals confirmed done around $3.70.
Revised forecasts anticipating warmer-than-expected temperatures throughout most of the Midwest was the major factor leading to the sharp drop in prices, traders said.
Adding to the softening was the drop in demand expected over the holiday.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were down an average of 45 cents from Friday to the high-$3.70s. Shortly before nomination deadlines, gas was selling in the $3.60s, traders said.
At the southern California border, prices softened by about five cents to the $4.15-4.20 range, with early deals confirmed done as high as the high-$4.30s.
Lending support to the California market were the strong domestic Canadian prices in Alberta due to the severely cold weather, resulting in prices around C$3 per gigajoule.
